title: Anybody Headed Down Today?
intro: Word is Priya's out on the green in Jefferson, asking if anybody's driving down to the city today. Hannah at Stewart's heard it first.
smallTalk: Priya's kid has a big show in the city tonight — I hope somebody's headed down that way.
Priya's been carrying that costume bag around under one arm all morning.
Tops finally got the good peaches in.
This has been the soggiest summer anybody up here can remember, and everybody's got an opinion about it.
Half the county's heard about Priya's kid's costume bag by now.
Somebody's always driving down to the city on a Sunday, if you ask around enough.
Word travels faster than traffic on Route 10, and that's saying something.
I hope that costume makes it there in one piece — I heard it's got sequins.
Walt's truck could use a wash before it goes anywhere near the city.
Nice to see everybody pitching in for Priya's kid.

lines: He texted a photo from the stage door the second he got it — you'll just have to imagine it, but trust me, it's a whole look.
Thank you, truly.
Still asking around? Try the gas station — half the county passes through there before nine.
Renata might know something — Cellar Door, down in Hobart.
Hannah's over at Stewart's, in Stamford — start there if you haven't yet.
My kid's in a dance showcase in the city tonight, and half his costume is in this bag.
I'm due back at the register at Middle Brook by four, or I'd drive it down myself. Here — take it, would you?
If you hear of anybody headed down today, ask them for me. Hannah's behind the counter at Stewart's, down in Stamford; she hears everybody's plans before they make them.
Tell me that bag made it to the stage door in one piece.
Renata sent you to Walt, then — J&H, the gas station up in Jefferson.
Nobody from in here's going down today, far as I know.
Check the board at Tops on your way through — and Cellar Door in Hobart, Renata always seems to know who's coming and going.
Morning! Coffee's on, and the sundae bar's real, if you're curious.
Priya called down from Jefferson asking if anybody's driving to the city today — she's out on the green up there, if you're headed that way.
Glad it worked out. Come by for a tasting sometime, once things settle down.
Go on, catch him before he leaves — the gas station, up in Jefferson.
Not me today — my truck's in the shop.
But I saw someone loading a cooler bag into their trunk up at the gas station this morning. Nobody packs a cooler for a trip up the road — that's a city run.
That'll be Walt — J&H, the gas station up in Jefferson.
Priya's costume run? Word travels. Not me today — my truck's in the shop.
Ask Hannah at the counter in Stewart's, up in Stamford; she'll know who was in this morning.
Welcome — pull up a seat on the bench anytime.
If you're headed up toward Jefferson, say hi to Priya on the green — I hear she's asking around about something.
Tell the kid break a leg from me. Had it there by six, like I said.
Priya's kid's costume? Sure — I'm headed down myself today, every other Sunday like clockwork.
Hand it over — I've got it. I'll get it to the stage door by six. Tell the kid break a leg.
Heard something's going around about a favor for Priya. Nothing solid on my end, but you never know who overhears what.
Every other Sunday I load up and head down for the week — traffic and all. Don't ask me why I keep doing it to myself.
If you're new around here, Priya's out on the green — good person to know.

steps.toast: Episode complete — new story next week

lines: Taped by the register: "Anybody headed down today? Ask around!" Half the county's already heard.
Pinned to the board by the door: someone's asking if anybody's headed down to the city today. Half the county's seen it already.
